newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares at new record close, off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares at new record close, off highs.

text.p: The market index at Istanbul's stock exchange closed at a new all-time high of 88,079.86 amid continued selective buying on Monday, but fell from an afternoon high of 89,218 on profit-taking, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 leapt 1,095.93 points, or 1.26 percent from Friday and compared to Thursday's previous record of 87,299.29. It had jumped 5.38 percent last week, toppling the stiff 85,000 barrier in the market's fourth attempt since late October.
Trade volume leapt to 26.24 trillion lira ($261.1 million) from 22.65 trillion ($227 million) on Friday.
"Technically, the market's first target is at one dollar and the second one at $1.3," said Resat Kutucular from Toros securities.
In dollar terms, the index stood at $0.88 on Monday, compared to a $1 record on April 8 and $0.67 at end-1995.
Some brokers said positive developments on the economic front, particulary progress in privatisation might be needed to fuel market expectations to support the uptrend.
